advances:
For the exact \(A_0\) calibration of accepted fact
`331355cde8383f52`, no single convex \(A_2\) can simultaneously have
the central common-order \(Q\)-support, strictly dominate the three
\(A_0\) traces, and admit positive middle-cell budgets satisfying the
\(k\)- and \(\ell\)-crossing equations.  The obstruction is exact:
the two adjacent boundary chords force
\[
|Q_{jk}|>\frac12\cdot\frac1{10}\cdot\frac1{46}
=\frac1{920},
\]
whereas the two crossings force
\[
|Q_{jk}|<|P_\ell|=\frac1{920}.
\]
Thus this calibration fails before the support-gap condition, the third
crossing, or \(W=0\) can be imposed.  The sharp chord lemma
`6a9cc7c11e208bba` is applied cyclically to both endpoints; its
inequalities are necessary but the adjacent-chord hull gives the strict
incompatibility.
author: mp_r90_opposite_support_gap_full_hypotheses
proof:
We first record the cyclic consequences of the sharp chord lemma
`6a9cc7c11e208bba`.  For \(A_0\), the central cell is \(P_0\), the
coordinate sum is \(\delta=3/2\), and the areas below
\(p_j=0,p_k=0,p_\ell=0\) are \(a,d,c+d\).  Thus the three inequalities
are
\[
a\left(b-\frac32\lambda_{0j}\right)_+
\le\frac{9\lambda_{0j}^2}{16},
\tag{7j}
\]
\[
d\left(b-\frac32\lambda_{0k}\right)_+
\le\frac{9\lambda_{0k}^2}{16},
\tag{7k}
\]
\[
(c+d)\left(b-\frac32\lambda_{0\ell}\right)_+
\le\frac{9\lambda_{0\ell}^2}{16}.
\tag{7l}
\]
For the values (1)-(2), these read
\[
\frac{693}{113600}<\frac9{256},\qquad
\frac{1167}{56285600}<\frac9{33856},\qquad
\frac{117}{266000}<\frac9{1600}.
\tag{8}
\]

Apply the same lemma to \(A_2\) with the three coordinates in (3).
The central cell \(Q_N\) lies in
\[
0<u<\tau,\qquad 0<w<\tau,\qquad 0<v<\tau.
\]
Under the support (4)-(5), the areas below \(u=0,w=0,v=0\) are,
respectively,
\[
s,\qquad e,\qquad e+g_0.
\]
Therefore
\[
s(g-\tau\lambda_{2j})_+
\le\frac{\lambda_{2j}^2\tau^2}{4},
\tag{9j}
\]
\[
e(g-\tau\lambda_{2k})_+
\le\frac{\lambda_{2k}^2\tau^2}{4},
\tag{9k}
\]
\[
(e+g_0)(g-\tau\lambda_{2\ell})_+
\le\frac{\lambda_{2\ell}^2\tau^2}{4}.
\tag{9l}
\]
These are the three cyclic \(A_2\) chord inequalities.  The contradiction
below is stronger than (9j)-(9l).

We next locate the two full boundary chords of \(Q_{jk}\).  Every
positive-area exact cell contains an interior point of \(A_2\) in its
strict sign chamber.  Consider a point of
\[
A_2\cap\{v=0\}.
\]
If it had \(w<0\), then \(u=\tau-w>0\).  Moving slightly toward an
interior point of \(Q_N\) would produce interior points with
\[
u>0,\qquad v>0,\qquad w<0,
\]
in the unsupported chamber \(Q_{j\ell}\).  If it had \(u<0\), then
\(w=\tau-u>0\).  Moving slightly toward an interior point of \(Q_{jk}\)
would produce interior points with
\[
u<0,\qquad v<0,\qquad w>0,
\]
in the unsupported chamber \(Q_k\).  Hence the whole chord satisfies
\[
u\ge0,\qquad w\ge0.
\tag{10}
\]

Now consider a point of
\[
A_2\cap\{w=0\}.
\]
If it had \(v>0\), move slightly toward an interior point of \(Q_j\).
The perturbed point has \(v>0,w<0\); according to the sign of \(u\),
it lies in the unsupported chamber \(Q_{j\ell}\) or \(Q_\ell\).
Thus \(v\le0\).  Since \(u+v=\tau>0\), this also gives \(u>0\).
Therefore the whole chord satisfies
\[
u\ge0,\qquad v\le0.
\tag{11}
\]

The positive areas on both sides of each cutting line show that
\(v=0\) and \(w=0\) meet \(\operatorname{int}A_2\).  Hence the
one-sided traces equal the actual full chord lengths.

Map the closed cell \(\overline{Q_{jk}}\) to the nonnegative quadrant by
\[
(r,t)=(w,-v).
\]
The map has determinant magnitude \(1\).  Its image \(D\) is compact
and convex, lies in \(\mathbb R_{\ge0}^2\), and has
\[
|D|=g_0.
\tag{12}
\]
Equations (10)-(11) and chord continuity give axis intervals
\[
D\cap\{r=0\}
=\{0\}\times[t_0,t_1],
\qquad
t_1-t_0=\lambda_{2k},
\tag{13}
\]
\[
D\cap\{t=0\}
=[r_0,r_1]\times\{0\},
\qquad
r_1-r_0=\lambda_{2\ell},
\tag{14}
\]
with all endpoints nonnegative.  Convexity puts the hull of these two
intervals inside \(D\).  Its area is
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac12(r_1t_1-r_0t_0)
&=\frac12\bigl(
r_0(t_1-t_0)+t_0(r_1-r_0)\\
&\hspace{23mm}+(r_1-r_0)(t_1-t_0)
\bigr)\\
&\ge\frac12\lambda_{2k}\lambda_{2\ell}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{15}
\]
Using the strict inequalities in (6),
\[
g_0
\ge\frac12\lambda_{2k}\lambda_{2\ell}
>
\frac12\cdot\frac1{46}\cdot\frac1{10}
=\frac1{920}
=c.
\tag{16}
\]

It remains to compare (16) with the crossings.  In the central
common-order support, write
\[
z=|R_N|,\qquad \omega=|R_{k\ell}|,
\]
and denote the common crossing value by \(\theta\).  The
\(k\)-crossing has the form
\[
d+(g_0+g+s)+(y+z+\omega)=\theta,
\tag{17}
\]
while the \(\ell\)-crossing is
\[
(c+d)+(g+s)+(z+\omega)=\theta.
\tag{18}
\]
Subtracting (18) from (17) gives
\[
c=g_0+y.
\tag{19}
\]
Since \(y>0\), equation (19) gives \(g_0<c\), contradicting (16).

Thus no \(A_2\) satisfying (3)-(6) can support the two crossing
equations.  This contradiction precedes, and therefore rules out,
any additional third crossing, \(W=0\), midpoint-containment, or
positive support-gap requirement.
statement:
Use the exact common-plane calibration of accepted fact
`331355cde8383f52`.  In the \(A_0\) coordinates
\[
X=p_j,\qquad Y=p_\ell,\qquad
p_k=\frac32-X-Y,
\]
the determinant magnitude is \(\Delta=1\), and the only positive
\(P\)-cells have areas
\[
a=|P_j|=\frac{21}{568},\qquad
b=|P_0|=\frac{27}{50},\qquad
c=|P_\ell|=\frac1{920},\qquad
d=|P_{k\ell}|=\frac1{24472}.
\tag{1}
\]
Their three coordinate chord traces are
\[
\lambda_{0j}=\frac14,\qquad
\lambda_{0k}=\frac1{46},\qquad
\lambda_{0\ell}=\frac1{10}.
\tag{2}
\]

For a proposed \(A_2\), put
\[
u=-q_j,\qquad v=-q_\ell,\qquad w=-q_k,
\qquad u+v+w=\tau=\frac72.
\tag{3}
\]
For \(H\subseteq N=\{j,k,\ell\}\), define
\[
Q_H=
A_2\cap
\{r_i\ge0\ (i\in H),\ r_i<0\ (i\notin H)\},
\qquad
(r_j,r_k,r_\ell)=(u,w,v).
\tag{4}
\]
Assume the only positive-area \(Q\)-cells are
\[
Q_j,\qquad Q_{jk},\qquad Q_N,\qquad Q_{k\ell},
\]
with respective areas
\[
e,\qquad g_0,\qquad g,\qquad s,
\tag{5}
\]
and assume all four are positive.  Let
\(\lambda_{2j},\lambda_{2k},\lambda_{2\ell}\) be the one-sided
coordinate chord traces at \(u=0,w=0,v=0\), respectively, and assume
strict trace domination:
\[
\lambda_{2j}>\frac14,\qquad
\lambda_{2k}>\frac1{46},\qquad
\lambda_{2\ell}>\frac1{10}.
\tag{6}
\]

Suppose a positive central common-order middle budget has
\[
y=|R_{jk}|>0
\]
and that its \(k\)- and \(\ell\)-crossing equations hold.  Then no such
\(A_2\) exists.  Consequently there is no exact rational \(A_2\), no
compatible middle completion satisfying all three crossings and \(W=0\),
and no such completion preserving any positive support-gap direction.
